accountMap.title: System account mapping
accountMap.intro: Accounts the system uses when it creates journals automatically. Change them only if your chart differs; changes apply to new transactions.

receivable.label: Accounts receivable
receivable.body: Customer control account. Every invoice and receipt is booked here per customer.

payable.label: Accounts payable
payable.body: Vendor control account. Every bill and payment is booked here per vendor.

vat_payable.label: VAT payable
vat_payable.body: Receives output minus input VAT on VAT settlement when tax is owed.

vat_overpaid.label: VAT overpaid
vat_overpaid.body: Receives the VAT balance on settlement when input exceeds output VAT.

employee_payable.label: Employee claims payable
employee_payable.body: Holds approved expense claims until they are paid.

retained_earnings.label: Retained earnings
retained_earnings.body: Receives net income (loss) when the fiscal year is closed.

opening_equity.label: Opening balance equity
opening_equity.body: Offsets opening balances entered for the first time.

fx_gain.label: FX gain
fx_gain.body: Exchange gains on settlement or revaluation of foreign currency.

fx_loss.label: FX loss
fx_loss.body: Exchange losses on settlement or revaluation of foreign currency.

rounding.label: Rounding difference
rounding.body: Holds small rounding residues (max. 1) so foreign-currency journals balance.

bank_fee.label: Bank charges
bank_fee.body: Admin or transfer fees deducted by the bank on receipts or payments.

asset_gain.label: Gain on asset disposal
asset_gain.body: Gain when a fixed asset is sold above its book value.

asset_loss.label: Loss on asset disposal
asset_loss.body: Loss when a fixed asset is sold or written off below its book value.

sales_revenue.label: Sales revenue
sales_revenue.body: Default revenue account for invoice lines without an item that has its own account.

purchase_expense.label: Default purchase account
purchase_expense.body: Default account for bill lines without an item that has its own account.

currencies.title: Currencies
currencies.codeHint: Three-letter ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD. Cannot be changed once saved.

terms.title: Payment terms
terms.daysHint: Due date = document date + this many days.

matrix.title: Role permission matrix
matrix.intro: Default access of each role per module. Per-user overrides can change this.
matrix.legend: C = create, R = read, U = update/process, D = delete/close.

guide.intro: Who does what in FinDesk and the everyday workflows. Every card links to its module.

admin.title: Admin
admin.body: Full access: company settings, users and permissions, account mapping, and reopening closed periods or fiscal years.

manager.title: Finance Manager
manager.body: Approves journals, bills, payments and expense claims; closes periods; reads every report and the audit trail; edits company settings.

accountant.title: Accountant
accountant.body: Maintains the chart of accounts, journals, tax, fixed assets, budgets and bank reconciliation; processes invoices and bills; approves other people's documents.

staff.title: Finance Staff
staff.body: Creates invoices, bills, receipts, payments and cash transactions and submits them. Can view journals and reports but cannot approve.

auditor.title: Auditor
auditor.body: Read-only: every module, the financial reports and the audit trail. Cannot change anything.

employee.title: Employee
employee.body: Submits and tracks their own expense claims only.

sales.title: Sales cycle
items: Make sure the customer exists under Customers & vendors, with tax ID and payment terms.
Create a sales invoice: enter lines and pick VAT 12% (DPP 11/12); the server computes totals.
Post the invoice. If it exceeds the customer's credit limit it waits for approval.
Record the receipt when the customer pays and allocate it to invoices; enter any tax withheld by the customer.
Watch receivables aging and follow up overdue invoices.

purchases.title: Purchase cycle
items: Enter the vendor bill from the original document; set PPh 23/4(2) on the line when you withhold it.
Submit the bill; amounts above the approval threshold need someone else's approval.
Plan payments from payables aging and the dashboard cash forecast.
Create the vendor payment, allocate it to bills, then post it.
Use a debit note for returns or price corrections instead of editing a posted bill.

cash.title: Cash & bank
items: Record cash in and cash out that do not come from invoices or bills (e.g. utilities, bank interest).
Use account transfers to move funds, including petty cash top-ups.
Foreign-currency accounts are booked at the day's rate; the rupiah balance follows the transaction rate.
Cash out above the approval threshold waits for approval before posting.
Check physical cash and bank statements against the books regularly.

reconcile.title: Bank reconciliation
items: Import or type the bank statement for one account and one period.
Match every bank line with a book transaction.
Book lines missing from the books directly, such as admin fees or interest.
Make sure the bank and book balances differ by zero, then finish the reconciliation.

tax.title: Tax
items: VAT 12% is computed on a DPP of 11/12 of the selling price (effectively 11%) per PMK 131/2024; luxury goods use the full DPP.
Enter the tax invoice number after the invoice is posted.
PPh 23 (services 2%) and PPh 4(2) (e.g. rent 10%) are withheld on bill lines and become tax payable.
PPh 21 is booked as tax payable from payroll and paid monthly.
At period end, run VAT settlement to move output and input VAT into payable or overpaid.
Use the VAT and withholding reports as the basis for monthly tax returns.

assets.title: Assets & depreciation
items: Register fixed assets with category, cost, in-service date and useful life.
Choose straight line or double declining balance.
Run depreciation every period; skipped months are caught up automatically.
Check the depreciation schedule for book value per month.
Record a disposal when an asset is sold or written off; gain/loss comes from book value.

closing.title: Monthly close
items: Post this month's recurring journals (rent, amortisation, accruals).
Run fixed-asset depreciation for the period.
Finish the reconciliation of every bank account.
Run VAT settlement for the tax period.
Run the month-end FX revaluation for foreign-currency balances.
Review the period checklist, then close the period; submitted documents block closing.

approval.title: Approval (maker-checker)
items: The creator of a document can never approve it.
Manual journals (when required), bills and payments above the threshold, invoices over the credit limit and every expense claim go to the queue.
Approvers open Approvals, check the details, then approve or reject with a reason.
Rejected documents return to draft for the creator to fix.
Status changes of invoices, bills, payments, cash and claims are recorded in the audit trail.

reports.title: Reports
items: The balance sheet shows the position at a date; the check line Assets = Liabilities + Equity must be zero.
The income statement can be filtered by cost center or project and compared with another period.
The cash flow uses the indirect method and ties to the closing cash balance.
The trial balance proves debits equal credits; click an account to open its ledger.
Export to Excel/CSV/PDF or print straight from every report.
